request.query: For arbitrary real C D b r and positive p, b<r implies there exists delta0 positive such that C*delta^p+b+D*delta<r for all 0<=delta<=delta0

      "informal_name": "Akra-Bazzi Recurrence Inequality for Critical Exponent and Smoothing Function",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] {T : ℕ → ℝ} {g : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : α → ℝ} {r : α → ℕ → ℕ} [inst_1 : Nonempty α]\n  (R : AkraBazziRecurrence T g a b r),\n  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,\n    ∀ (i : α),\n      ↑(r i n) ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * (1 - AkraBazziRecurrence.smoothingFn ↑(r i n)) ≤\n        b i ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * ↑n ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * (1 - AkraBazziRecurrence.smoothingFn ↑n)",

      "informal_description": "A function $ f : \\mathbb{R} \\to \\mathbb{R} $ satisfies the polynomial growth condition if, for every $ b \\in (0, 1) $, there exist positive constants $ c_1 $ and $ c_2 $ such that for sufficiently large $ x $, and for all $ u \\in [b x, x] $, the inequality $ c_1 f(x) \\leq f(u) \\leq c_2 f(x) $ holds.",

      "kind": "theorem",

      "informal_description": "For any real constant $c < 1$, there exists some $N$ such that for all $x > N$, the inequality $c < 1 - \\frac{1}{\\ln x}$ holds. This describes the asymptotic behavior of the smoothing function $\\varepsilon(x) = \\frac{1}{\\ln x}$ in the Akra-Bazzi method.",

    {

Then for any real number $b$ with $0 < b < 1$, there exists a positive constant $c$ such that for all sufficiently large $x$, and for all $u$ in the closed interval $[b \\cdot x, x]$, we have $f(u) \\le c \\cdot f(x)$.",

items.informal_name: Akra-Bazzi Recurrence Inequality for Critical Exponent and Smoothing Function
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] {T : ℕ → ℝ} {g : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : α → ℝ} {r : α → ℕ → ℕ} [inst_1 : Nonempty α]
  (R : AkraBazziRecurrence T g a b r),
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (i : α),
      ↑(r i n) ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * (1 - AkraBazziRecurrence.smoothingFn ↑(r i n)) ≤
        b i ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * ↑n ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * (1 - AkraBazziRecurrence.smoothingFn ↑n)
items.informal_description: For all sufficiently large natural numbers $ n $ and for all $ i $ in the finite type $ \alpha $, the inequality $ (r(i,n))^p \cdot (1 - \varepsilon(r(i,n))) \leq (b(i))^p \cdot n^p \cdot (1 - \varepsilon(n)) $ holds, where $ p $ is the critical exponent satisfying $ \sum_{i \in \alpha} a_i (b_i)^p = 1 $, $ r(i,n) $ defines the recurrence's index mapping, and $ \varepsilon $ represents a small positive function related to the smoothing term $ 1/\ln(n) $.

items.informal_name: Eventual Inequality for Akra-Bazzi Recurrence with Critical Exponent $ p $ and Smoothing Function
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] {T : ℕ → ℝ} {g : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : α → ℝ} {r : α → ℕ → ℕ} [inst_1 : Nonempty α]
  (R : AkraBazziRecurrence T g a b r),
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (i : α),
      b i ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * ↑n ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * (1 + AkraBazziRecurrence.smoothingFn ↑n) ≤
        ↑(r i n) ^ AkraBazziRecurrence.p a b * (1 + AkraBazziRecurrence.smoothingFn ↑(r i n))
items.informal_description: For all sufficiently large natural numbers $ n $, and for all indices $ i $, the inequality $ b_i^p n^p (1 + \varepsilon(n)) \leq (r_i(n))^p (1 + \varepsilon(r_i(n))) $ holds, where $ p $ is the critical exponent satisfying $ \sum_{i \in \alpha} a_i b_i^p = 1 $, $ \varepsilon(n) $ is the smoothing function $ 1/\ln n $, and $ r_i(n) $ represents the recurrence's index mapping.

items.informal_name: Polynomial Growth Condition for Akra-Bazzi Recurrence
items.informal_description: A function $ f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfies the polynomial growth condition if, for every $ b \in (0, 1) $, there exist positive constants $ c_1 $ and $ c_2 $ such that for sufficiently large $ x $, and for all $ u \in [b x, x] $, the inequality $ c_1 f(x) \leq f(u) \leq c_2 f(x) $ holds.

items.informal_name: Smoothing Function Eventually Greater Than Constants Less Than One
items.type: ∀ c < 1, ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, c < 1 - AkraBazziRecurrence.smoothingFn x
items.informal_description: For any real constant $c < 1$, there exists some $N$ such that for all $x > N$, the inequality $c < 1 - \frac{1}{\ln x}$ holds. This describes the asymptotic behavior of the smoothing function $\varepsilon(x) = \frac{1}{\ln x}$ in the Akra-Bazzi method.

items.informal_name: Polynomial Growth Implies an Eventual Upper Bound
items.type:
∀ {f : ℝ → ℝ} {b : ℝ},
  b ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 →
    AkraBazziRecurrence.GrowsPolynomially f →
      ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ u ∈ Set.Icc (b * x) x, f u ≤ c * f x
items.informal_description: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function that satisfies the polynomial growth condition. Then for any real number $b$ with $0 < b < 1$, there exists a positive constant $c$ such that for all sufficiently large $x$, and for all $u$ in the closed interval $[b \cdot x, x]$, we have $f(u) \le c \cdot f(x)$.

items.informal_name: Eventual Lower Bound for Polynomial Growth in Akra-Bazzi Recurrence
items.type:

items.informal_description: If a function $ f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfies the polynomial growth condition, then for every $ b \in (0, 1) $, there exists a positive constant $ c $ such that for sufficiently large $ x $, and for all $ u \in [b x, x] $, the inequality $ c f(x) \leq f(u) $ holds.
